findings.excerpt:
have hai : a i ∈ Metric.ball x ε := by
        rw [Metric.mem_ball, Real.dist_eq, abs_lt]
        constructor <;> linarith [hi.1, hi.2]
findings.problem: The non-prevertex branch builds the open set `hopen`, then restates the interval membership by hand. It passes through `Metric.ball`, `Real.dist_eq` and `abs_lt` and uses `linarith` three times to convert between `Metric.ball x ε` and `Ioo (x - ε) (x + ε)`. Mathlib already has `Real.ball_eq_Ioo`, which says exactly `ball x r = Ioo (x - r) (x + r)`. The intermediate `hopen`, `hxIoo` and `ha` haves are each used only once.
findings.proposed_change:
Rewrite the ball as an interval once and pass the avoidance fact directly:
```
  · obtain ⟨ε, hε, hball⟩ :=
      Metric.isOpen_iff.mp (Set.finite_range a).isClosed.isOpen_compl x hx
    rw [Real.ball_eq_Ioo] at hball
    obtain ⟨L, hL, -, -⟩ := exists_tendsto_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive_sub_eq a e z₀
      (p := x - ε) (q := x + ε) fun i _ hi => hball hi ⟨i, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨L x, hL x ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩⟩
```
The argument is the same: the prevertices form a closed set avoiding `x`, so a whole interval around `x` has no prevertex, and the edge continuation applies.
findings.benefit: The proof drops about ten lines and the metric-to-order conversion with `abs_lt`. A reader sees the idea directly: a neighbourhood interval of `x` avoids `range a`, so the edge lemma applies.

convert hLcol using 1
  ext z
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨x, hx, (schwarzChristoffelBoundary_eq_of_tendsto a e z₀ x (hL x hx)).symm⟩
findings.problem: The proof shows the two images are equal by a manual `ext`, a `constructor`, and two `rintro`/`exact` blocks. The map and `L` agree pointwise on `Ioo p q`, because `schwarzChristoffelBoundary_eq_of_tendsto` gives `boundary x = L x`. Equal images of agreeing functions is exactly `Set.image_congr`.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the body after the `obtain` with a single rewrite:
```
  rw [Set.image_congr (g := L) fun x hx =>
    schwarzChristoffelBoundary_eq_of_tendsto a e z₀ x (hL x hx)]
  exact hLcol
```
The proof now says directly that the boundary map and `L` agree on the interval, so their images agree and collinearity transfers.
findings.benefit: This removes the `convert … using 1`, the `ext`, and the duplicated two-direction membership proof. The remaining step is the pointwise agreement that the mathematics uses.
